items.title: Academy Museum Gala 2026 Red Carpet: Taylor Swift, Inde Navarrette, Kate Hudson and More
items.summary:
The Academy Museum of Motion Pictures held its sixth annual gala, drawing one of the larger concentrations of film and music celebrity Los Angeles sees in a given year and raising more than $14 million for the museum. Taylor Swift performed during the evening and was among those on the red carpet, alongside Jessica Biel and Justin Timberlake, Kim Kardashian, Jacob Elordi, Kendall Jenner, Eva Longoria, Salma Hayek, Nia Long, McKenna Grace, Rosé, Sabrina Carpenter, Janelle Monáe, Pamela Anderson, Charles Melton and Alexander Skarsgård.

The program centered on three honors. Charlize Theron received the Icon Award, Colman Domingo took the Vantage Award, and John Carpenter was given the Luminary Award. Carpenter attended with Sandy King.

Rolex presented the gala, which Robert Rodriguez, Steven Spielberg and Kate Capshaw, and Tom Ford co-chaired. The host committee ran long and deep into both the acting and filmmaking ranks: Jessica Alba, Judd Apatow and Leslie Mann, Autumn Durald Arkapaw, Adrien Brody and Georgina Chapman, Jon M. Chu, Kirsten Dunst, Nicholas Galitzine, Ludwig and Serena Göransson, Regina Hall, Kate Hudson, Jessica Lange, Greta Lee, John Legend and Chrissy Teigen, Rami Malek, Demi Moore, Olivia Munn, Gina Prince-Bythewood, Questlove, Da'Vine Joy Randolph, Seth Rogen and Lauren Miller Rogen, Bird Runningwater and Teyana Taylor.

Variety photographed the arrivals, which included Gabrielle Union and Dwyane Wade, Goldie Hawn and Kurt Russell, Dakota and Elle Fanning, Ross and Matt Duffer, Jason Reitman with Josephine Reitman, Slash with Meegan Hodges, Amber Valletta with Jason Wu, Javier Ambrossi and Javier Calvó, Stephen Root and Romy Rosemont, and Academy CEO Bill Kramer with Peter Cipkowski.

The fundraising total marks another year of the gala functioning as the museum's principal annual revenue event, five years after the institution opened on Wilshire Boulevard. Inde Navarrette, Connor Storrie and Drew Starkey were also among the expected attendees on the carpet.

items.title: Harry Styles ‘Together, Together’ Tour Doc Coming From John Wilson, Universal Pictures Content Group (EXCLUSIVE)
items.summary:
Harry Styles has handed documentary filmmaker John Wilson access to his Madison Square Garden residency, with cameras rolling on the singer since August. Variety reported the project exclusively, citing two sources with knowledge of it, and said Universal Pictures Content Group, Peanut World Pictures and Styles himself are producing.

Wilson is best known for the HBO series "How To with John Wilson" and the independent box-office surprise "The History of Concrete," both built on close observation of ordinary life. The Styles film is described as a hybrid of concert footage and a look at the world around the tour, with one source characterizing it as centering on the people involved at every level, from the singer and his audience to the crew working behind the stage.

Universal Pictures Content Group will hold global rights. Distribution has not been locked, though insiders told Variety the documentary may be steered toward a theatrical run through Universal. Representatives for Styles, Wilson and Universal did not immediately comment.

The residency is the largest single-engagement run ever staged at Madison Square Garden and forms the core of Styles' "Together, Together" tour. It opened in late August and runs through the end of October. Word of the documentary spread after a fan photographed Wilson following Styles with a camera over the weekend.

Wilson is an unusual fit for a pop concert film on paper, but the category has been absorbing idiosyncratic directors for a while now. Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Elizabeth Holmes documentary "You Can See Everything" is performing well in specialty release, and Billie Eilish brought in James Cameron to direct "Hit Me Hard and Soft: The Tour," which played theaters this summer.

Wilson started out directing music videos and is represented by UTA. Shooting continues through the remainder of the MSG dates.

items.title: London Film Festival: Sergei Loznitsa’s ‘Imperium’ & Sompot Chidgasornpongse’s ‘9 Temples To Heaven’ Among Big Winners — Full List
items.summary:
Sergei Loznitsa's "Imperium" won Best Film in the Official Competition at the London Film Festival, which announced its prizes on the festival's closing day. The Ukrainian director's latest assembles archival material into a portrait of the Soviet Union in the early 1970s.

Documentary filmmaker Sam Pollard led the Official Competition jury, which called the film an "extraordinary film that explores the Soviet Union in the early 1970's from a rich archive with a wide-ranging perspective that looks at life in a country with an extraordinary social and cultural landscape that has rarely been seen." The jury added that the picture is "richly evocative and emotionally engaging on all levels," and said it was "immensely proud to honour such a powerful and singular piece of work."

Thai director Sompot Chidgasornpongse took the Sutherland Award in the First Feature Competition for "9 Temples To Heaven," which premiered at Cannes. The film follows Sakol, who undertakes a single-day pilgrimage to nine temples after hearing a prophecy that his elderly mother may soon die. Kissada Kamyoung and Apichatpong Weerasethakul produced, with Thomas Hakim and Julien Graff of petit chaos — the company behind Payal Kapadia's "All We Imagine as Light" — co-producing.

The first feature jury, chaired by Amir El-Masry, described the film as an "accomplished first feature paving his own path in the well-established tradition of filmmaking in the Southeast Asian region," calling it "visually outstanding, spiritual, and meditative, where a story about life and death transcends borders and generations."

In the remaining categories, Asmahan Bkerat's "Concrete Land" won the Grierson Award in the Documentary Competition and Rahul Roye's "Aman" took the Short Film Award, according to Deadline. The festival closes this evening with a screening of "The Debut," directed by Jesse Eisenberg.
